title: Orchestrate cohorted control plane rollouts with version pinning and automated rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Automate safe, auditable control plane version upgrades for Private (VPC) customers by orchestrating cohorted canary rollouts, customer-scoped version pinning, and automated rollback on health regressions.

Background: Private control planes must upgrade without violating tenant isolation or SLAs. Previous ad-hoc upgrades required manual gating and poor visibility. This ticket standardizes the upgrade pipeline (Terraform + operator hooks) to run deterministic, observable cohorts with automatic remediation.

Success criteria:
- Define cohort selection strategy (by customer size, region, or explicit opt-in) and ability to pin a customer to a specific control-plane version.
- Terraform modules expose canary_count, cohort_selector, and pre/post-apply health check hooks.
- Automated promotion logic that promotes from cohort -> majority when metrics are stable for N windows, otherwise triggers automated rollback and alerting.
- Rollback runbook + automated rollback Terraform path verified in staging and one pilot customer.
- Telemetry: 99.9% of rollouts report health metrics; error-rate increase detection threshold and latency regressions are enforced.

Approach:
1) Terraform: add an upgrades module at terraform/modules/controlplane/upgrade that creates a new controlplane-version resource and cohort targeting labels (customer_namespace, region, size). The module will wire pre/post hooks to call the health-check Lambda or k8s job.
2) Control plane operator: support dual-running versions per cluster (old/new) with traffic-slicing via service mesh annotation. Implement graceful KV migration detection and staged schema migration flag.
3) Orchestration service: a small controller (go) that evaluates SLO-based promotion rules, triggers Terraform applies via CI, and records decisions to the audit log (S3 + KMS).
4) Health checks: define canary probe set (smoke e2e, admin API latencies, reconciliation success, DB migration state). Integrate with existing obs pipelines (datadog dashboards, traces).
5) Runbook: document manual override and emergency rollback steps in Confluence (link below).

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Cohort size vs blast radius: smaller cohorts reduce risk but slow rollouts. Default cohort = 2 small customers + 1 medium for initial pilot.
- DB migrations: aim for non-blocking migrations; where impossible, add explicit migration gates and scheduled maintenance windows.
- Cost: dual-running versions increases infra temporarily. Track cost and auto-scale down after promotion.

Risks:
- Incomplete telemetry coverage for some private customers may block automated promotion; fallback to manual gating required.
- Edge-case third-party integrations with pinned versions may fail and require per-customer rollback.

Notes on observability: promotion decisions are recorded with full metric snapshots and artifact refs. Exposes a per-rollout dashboard link in the upgrade task log.

2025-02-20 Marco: Prototype terraform module pushed to feature branch: github.com/redwood/infra/compare/upgrade-cohorts. See PR #4862. Basic schema includes cohort_selector, pinned_version, pre_hook, post_hook. Needs reviews from infra and runtime teams.

2025-02-25 Ruth (runtime eng): Reviewed operator changes. Key feedback: operator must surface KV-cache warmup state; do not flip traffic until warmup completes. Filed feedback in PR comments and added integration test checklist.

2025-02-28 Marco: Integrated health-check job (k8s CronJob) and wired Datadog monitors. Simulated promotion in staging using 3 simulated tenants; observed 0.6% p50 latency bump during initial stage -- within threshold. Linked simulation results: https://datadog.redwood/simulations/rollout-20250228
2025-03-03 PM review (Jared Kim): Requested clearer rollback SLAs and runbook; added acceptance criteria for automated rollback within 5 minutes of threshold breach. Assigned runbook owner: Ruth.

2025-03-06 Marco: Implemented automated rollback path and smoke test gate. Terraform plan/app automation ready for canary pilot. Scheduling pilot with 2 pilot customers week of 2025-03-17. Opening follow-up tickets for customer opt-in UX and billing annotation.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes cohort_selector, pinned_version, pre_hook, post_hook and has unit tests.
Operator supports dual-running versions and exposes warmup/ready signals consumed by post_hook.
Orchestration service can evaluate promotion rules and perform automated promotion or rollback based on metrics windows.
Run a successful pilot upgrade against 3 staging tenants with promotion + rollback exercised and documented results.
Confluence runbook for manual overrides and emergency rollback published and linked to the ticket.
